hero.title: Nova Weather iOS Application
paragraphs: Nova Weather is a cross-platform weather application that began as a native iOS app built in Swift and was later rebuilt in Flutter to support both iOS and Android from a single codebase. Alongside the frontend migration, I rewrote the backend in Python to provide a cleaner, more flexible API layer for fetching and transforming weather data.

The project served as a practical exercise in re-architecting an existing product, balancing platform-specific performance with cross-platform maintainability, and designing a backend that could evolve alongside the client. Nova Weather reflects my interest in iterative development, API design, and building systems that can adapt as requirements change.

features.text: Initially Developed Using Swift, Then Ported
Backend Reworked for Ported Flutter Version
Hosted Flask Backend on Microsoft Azure

concepts.label: KEY CONCEPTS LEARNED
items: SwiftUI and Flutter encourage very different UI and state patterns.
Cross-platform apps trade native feel for faster iteration.
Rewriting the backend clarified API design and data flow.
A custom API gave more control than a managed backend.
Porting exposed architectural flaws in the original design.
Designing for change matters as much as shipping fast.

body.title: Project Overview
paragraphs: Image-In is a web application that allows users to drag and drop images and receive structured JSON data describing the detected content. The goal of the project was to explore image analysis workflows and build a clean, minimal interface around a technically complex process. I wanted the experience to feel instant and frictionless, while keeping the underlying system flexible enough to support different types of image processing and future AI integrations.

body.title: System Architecture & Implementation
paragraphs: The frontend was built using Next.js and React, with a focus on a simple drag-and-drop interaction model and clear visual feedback during uploads and processing. Images are sent to a custom C# API, which handles validation, processing, and communication with the image analysis pipeline.

I designed the API to return consistent, predictable JSON structures so the frontend could remain loosely coupled from backend implementation details. As the project evolved, I refactored the backend to improve separation of concerns and make it easier to extend analysis logic.

body.title: Key Learnings & Future Direction
paragraphs: This project highlighted the importance of clean API contracts and predictable data models when working with dynamic or AI-generated outputs. Designing for extensibility early made it significantly easier to experiment with new processing approaches without breaking the frontend. Future iterations of Image-In will focus on expanding analysis capabilities, improving result visualization, and adding user-level features such as saved histories and exportable datasets.
